caption: Avalanche saves the interest, snowball gives you wins faster. Which one would you have picked?

slides.title:
How I'm clearing
R64 000 of debt
on R21 800 p/m
Living in Port Shepstone
slides.body:
Male, 31
Single, no kids
Job: Pharmacy dispensing assistant
Net salary: R21 800 p/m
Debt: R64 000 across four accounts

slides.title: Debt repayments
slides.includes: Personal loan R2 900, credit card R1 800, clothing account R1 100, furniture R1 000
slides.body: Four accounts, four due dates. The personal loan is the biggest balance, the credit card has the highest interest.

slides.title: Rent
slides.body: I could live cheaper but it's five minutes from work and I walk.

slides.title: Groceries
slides.includes: Spar, Boxer, lunch packed from home
slides.body: I started packing lunch in March. It saves about R700 a month, which goes straight onto the card.

slides.title: Scooter & taxi
slides.includes: Petrol, insurance, taxi to Durban for visits
slides.body: The scooter is the best money I ever spent. It's also not paid off.

slides.title: Eating out
slides.includes: Fish and chips Fridays, rugby with the boys
slides.body: I cut this from R3 000. It still hurts every Friday.

slides.title: Everything else
slides.includes: Prepaid electricity, phone contract, funeral policy, stokvel, medical aid, gym
slides.body: The stokvel is R300 and I didn't pause it. The December payout is the one thing I'm not touching.

slides.title: What's left
slides.body: Out of R21 800. About R23 a day for the rest of the month. I've done the interest sums more times than I'd admit.

slides.title: I stopped guessing
slides.body:
I put all four debts into Beyond Horizon and compared avalanche and snowball side by side.

It shows the total interest for each, so I could see the gap.

No bank login needed.
